preamble: Raising the open nucleus of [ai] to mid [e] gives [ei]. This happened to the Proto-Germanic diphthong *ai in both North and West Germanic. Proto-Norse stainaʀ became Old Norse steinn, and in Old High German *ai became ei except before r, w and h (and word-finally), where it went further to ē. In unstressed syllables, Old Latin had merged *ai and *oi into ei by historical times, and this ei later became ī.

examples.note: Proto-Germanic *ai became ei; Old English stān and Gothic stains show other outcomes.
Most environments keep a diphthong, raised to ei.
Contrast: before h (and before r, w, and word-finally) *ai monophthongized to ē instead.
